canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across the papers, the prevailing usage treats this behavior as revising an existing plan, action sequence, preference, or strategy after new information arrives or conditions change. Most formulations center on feedback from the environment, task progress, user requirements, or other agents, and several make the revision concrete as adding, removing, or changing actions, or updating the plan after each executor step. A smaller line narrows the behavior to rewriting steps to satisfy a new condition, or adjusting specific sub-tasks rather than re-planning an entire workflow, and some travel work also expects the revised plan to remain coherent and feasible.

Variants. Variants span travel planning with revision cases across dining, transportation, budget, and weather-dependent activities, multi-agent dialogue where agents adjust just before action selection, and execution settings where plans are updated from current state, task progress, or validator feedback. Papers use several names for these variants, ranging from course correction and strategy revision to task-driven, dynamic, and counterfactual replanning.

Space of elicitation and scores. No measurement instrument is linked to it. Papers instead elicit it through scenario designs that introduce changed user needs or weather, new information from other agents, step-by-step execution feedback, or verification feedback, and some operationalizations make the revision observable through explicit action edits, such as adding, removing, or changing steps. Some travel work also treats coherence and feasibility under changed constraints as the target of a successful revision.

What it is taken as evidence of. The only linked construct is Adaptability. One paper claims a causal relationship from plan revision to Adaptability, describing task-driven re-planning as part of a system meant to enhance adaptability by adjusting to real-time feedback and exceptions. No other construct is linked here.

definitions.text: Modifying an existing travel plan in response to changes in user preferences or environmental conditions such as weather or transportation disruptions.
definitions.paper: RETAIL: Towards Real-world Travel Planning for Large Language Models

definitions.text: Agents revise an initial preference or plan after hearing other agents or receiving new information.
definitions.paper: The Hidden Strength of Disagreement: Unraveling the Consensus-Diversity Tradeoff in Adaptive Multi-Agent Systems

definitions.text: An adaptive planning strategy where an agent adjusts specific sub-tasks within a larger workflow in response to feedback, rather than re-planning the entire sequence from scratch.
definitions.paper: OSCAR: Operating System Control via State-Aware Reasoning and Re-Planning

definitions.text: The capacity of an agent to revise its high-level plan in response to real-time environmental feedback and unexpected changes during task execution.
definitions.paper: Plan-and-Act: Improving Planning of Agents for Long-Horizon Tasks

definitions.text: The latent ability of a model to dynamically adjust travel plans in response to changing user needs or external conditions, maintaining coherence and feasibility.
definitions.paper: RETAIL: Towards Real-world Travel Planning for Large Language Models

definitions.text: The dynamic modification of a pre-generated task plan in response to real-time application states and task progress.
definitions.paper: UICOMPASS: UI Map Guided Mobile Task Automation via Adaptive Action Generation

definitions.text: The observable pattern of altering a decision-making approach over repeated rounds based on feedback from previous outcomes.
definitions.paper: Noise, Adaptation, and Strategy: Assessing LLM Fidelity in Decision-Making

definitions.text: Rewriting an existing plan to satisfy a new condition or constraint, requiring revision of step sequences while preserving goal alignment.
definitions.paper: PlaSma: Procedural Knowledge Models for Language-based Planning and Re-Planning

definitions.text: Adjusting or revising a current action sequence based on environmental feedback to improve task performance.
definitions.paper: Hephaestus: Improving Fundamental Agent Capabilities of Large Language Models through Continual Pre-Training

definitions.text: The observable behavior of modifying a generated plan by adding, removing, or changing actions in response to feedback from a verification process.
definitions.paper: Hierarchical Planning for Complex Tasks with Knowledge Graph-RAG and Symbolic Verification

relationships.paper: OSCAR: Operating System Control via State-Aware Reasoning and Re-Planning
relationships.evidence: To enhance stability and adaptability, OSCAR operates as a state machine, equipped with error-handling mechanisms and task-driven re-planning, allowing it to efficiently adjust to real-time feedback and exceptions. (ABSTRACT)
